extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, program managers, patent and trademark examiners, and external stakeholders (policy makers, applicants, and international partners)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of organizational standards, performance indicators, training programs, and procedural requirements the USPTO uses to measure, manage, and improve patent and trademark examination quality, timeliness, data reliability, and international engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Office Professional Staff Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides webcast training to professional staff and new employees regarding the entire application process, focusing on the roles and responsibilities of individual business units throughout Trademarks, as well as an overview of the trademark examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is intended to instruct examining attorneys on administrative processes and procedures specific to examination of trademark applications and to improve their role as examining attorneys. Offered as part of ongoing employee development.

rubrics_metrics.name: TM Talks Supervisor Training
rubrics_metrics.description: On-the-job training and development for Trademarks supervisors tailored specifically to Trademarks’ organizational goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual topics include merit system principles, labor relations, managing virtual employees, business processes, problem solving, project management, dealing with difficult situations. Sessions are held live, recorded for later viewing, and may include practical topics (OneNote use, performance action plan and position description writing, labor relations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership Journey Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarterly hour-long moderated sessions that highlight leadership stories and lessons learned from Trademarks and agency leaders to inspire and provide insights on serving as a leader at the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target audience includes current leaders, those who aspire to leadership, or those who lead without a formal title; leverages institutional knowledge and real-world experiences; sessions may be recorded and made available agency-wide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Service Units Training
rubrics_metrics.description: New employee training and ongoing educational training for legal instrument examiners and legal specialists in trademark service units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerings include Pre-Exam, Legal Instruments, Intent to Use, Madrid Processing, and Post Registration units to ensure unit-specific competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners' Annual Performance Agreements and Bonus Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual performance agreements between each Commissioner (Patents and Trademarks) and the Secretary of Commerce that outline measurable organizational goals and objectives for which they are responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bonuses (up to 50% of base salary subject to aggregate salary limits) may be awarded based on evaluations defined in the agreement; performance agreements should define measurable objectives and evaluation criteria; bonus outcomes reported in APPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of Performance Measures through Strategic and Annual Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance measures are developed through strategic planning and annual performance planning to ensure alignment with agency objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program managers document detailed information about each measure, including definitions, rationale, data sources, and data collection/computation methods to support transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Manager Confirmation of Data Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers must confirm that procedures are in place to ensure performance data are accurate and that measurement sources are complete and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers follow a standard reporting procedure to document performance measure definitions, rationale, data sources, and collection/computation methods; this confirmation is a control for data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT Solutions and Automated Monitoring for Data Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of automated systems and databases (e.g., Docket and Application Viewer, Official Correspondence, PALM, Trademark Reporting and Application Monitoring) that collect, track, and store performance indicators and incorporate internal edits to control data accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems evaluate data against expected results for reasonableness, consistency, and accuracy; cross-checks between internal systems and external expert monitoring provide additional assurances; product owners, Agile teams, and program managers jointly monitor systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Reviews and OCFO Oversight of Performance Data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Chief Financial Officer monitors agency performance, providing direction and support on data collection methodology and analysis and ensuring data quality checks are in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCFO periodically reviews processes and internal controls over verification and validation of performance measures in collaboration with program managers and reports findings; results of reviews inform improvements to measurement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic Verification and Validation of Performance Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodic verification and validation activities to ensure quality, reliability, and credibility of performance measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At fiscal year start and during reporting periods, USPTO reviews and adjusts sampling techniques and counts to ensure statistical reliability; teams conduct data analyses to identify statistically significant trends and underlying factors; adjustments made as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of Progress Toward Targets and Risk Mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing analysis of progress toward performance measurement targets and broader strategic goals, including discussion of program risks and development of mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include analyzing progress, identifying risks, and documenting mitigation plans to ensure reported performance data are complete, accurate, consistent, and reliable for intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Response and Implementation of Corrective Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to DOC OIG and GAO audits by implementing recommended corrective actions to mitigate findings (example: patent classification and routing processes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO concurs with recommendations and works with auditors to complete corrective actions by due dates; tracking of open recommendations and milestone completion is part of performance management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt to Emerging Technologies (AI and ET Actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy, technical, and outreach actions to advance and govern development and use of AI and other emerging technologies (ET) in the intellectual property ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes drafting AI policy, developing AI image search for design patents, developing NexGen ML for classification of utility applications, driving AI search output on patent documents, issuing guidance on GUIs, tracking prioritized ET programs and filings, testing ML models for classification transitions, and measuring business impacts and user acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Integrity of Patent and Trademark Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions to maintain integrity of the patent application system and the trademark register, including fraud monitoring and prevention and secure applicant identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes monitoring and preventing fraud in patent applications (utility, plant, design), providing secure digital identification (e.g., ID.me) for applicants, promptly publicizing policy changes, increasing clarity in AIA trial proceedings, expanding register protection teams, and public outreach to improve understanding of PTAB proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve Patent/Trademark Quality and Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic objectives to improve examination quality and reduce pendency through evidence-based practices, testing initiatives, training, surveys, and feedback integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include driving an evidence-based, problem-solving culture; testing initiatives identified by customers and examiners; expanding internal survey/data monitoring for examiner experience and infrastructure impacts; integrating stakeholder feedback; providing coaching/mentoring to increase technical and legal skills; measuring compliance with quality and pendency metrics; updating Master Review Form and sampling strategy for design patents; optimizing workflow with technology/training; and specific operational targets such as processing rocket docket (expedited design) applications within six months to first office action and achieving Hague Treaty compliance ≥93%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve Critical Mission Support Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen mission support via IT modernization, procurement practices, contractor evaluation, and cyber risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement audit recommendations (e.g., patent legacy systems), retire vulnerable legacy IT systems, prioritize cyber vulnerabilities in product development, include noncompetitive procurements in PTAG desktop guide, train customers on procurement planning, eliminate overdue CPARS evaluations, evaluate impacts of Patents Innovation Lab, and improve IT cost/schedule estimate documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total PTA Compliance — All Mailed Actions (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) compliance for mailed actions based on AIPA timeframes (14-4-4-4-36): time to issue office action, respond to reply/appeal, act after PTAB/federal court decision, issue patent after fee payment, and 36-month patent issuance timeframe exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports PTA for all mailed actions (office actions mailed to applicants); includes explanation of exceptions (interference/derivation proceedings, secrecy orders under 35 U.S.C. 181, appellate review durations) and offsets for applicant delays; target example FY2023 = 80% with actual 81% and status indicators (Met/Not Met/Exceeded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Total PTA Compliance — Remaining Inventory (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: PTA compliance measured for remaining inventory (cases awaiting action from the agency) using the same AIPA timeframes and exception rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports performance on remaining inventory separately from mailed actions; identifies drivers of pendency (attrition, reduced production, steady filing rates) and operational responses (overtime, examiner award revisions, increased hiring) to address inventory; includes targets, actuals, and status tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Statutory Compliance Metrics (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages measuring compliance with statutory requirements for patentability and specification (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112) based on Office of Patent Quality Assurance reviews of random samples of work products for compliance with Title 35 and relevant case law at time of determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics reported by statute (e.g., 101 utility/eligibility, 102 novelty/prior art compliance, 103 nonobviousness/prior art compliance, 112(a)/(b) specification related rejections including 112(f)); include targets and FY results (example FY2023 results: 101 — 98.2% vs target 94%; 102 — 96.0% vs 94%; 103 — 92.2% vs 91%; 112 — 94.4% vs 92%); used to evaluate examiner work quality and guide adjustments to targets and sampling strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Average First Action Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness of the first office action measured from application filing date (or 66(a) notification date) to the first office action, expressed in months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes historical context (pre-pandemic 2.5–3.5 months, surge during FY2020–2021), causes of backlog, and actions to reduce pendency; reports targets, actuals, and status (example FY2023 target and actual both 8.5 months; includes initiatives such as hiring, system modernization, and retiring legacy systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Average Total Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness of trademark application disposal measured from filing date to disposal (registration, abandonment, or notice of allowance), excluding suspended or inter partes proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports target/actual and historical trends, notes backlog effects on total pendency, and lists initiatives (hiring examining attorneys, paralegal support, publishing pendency widget, exploring efficiency improvements); example FY2023 actual 14.6 months vs target 14.5 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark First Action Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of all issues in making a first action substantive decision on registrability; evaluates quality based on decision-making, search strategy, evidence, and writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as a compliance percentage (example FY2023 compliance 96.8% vs target 95.5%); USPTO uses standardized training, feedback, online tools, and improved examination guidance to maintain quality; reported as outcome metric with targets and status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Final Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of all issues involved in making a final substantive decision on registrability; evaluates quality based on decision-making, search strategy, evidence, and writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as a compliance percentage (example FY2023 compliance 98.6% vs target 97.0%); tracked over time with targets and status, supports commitment to high-quality final office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Country Team Progress Metric (3-of-4 Criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of prioritized countries for which IP country teams have made progress on at least three of four specified performance criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four criteria are: (a) institutional improvements of IP office administration for advancing IP rights; (b) institutional improvements of IP enforcement entities; (c) improvements in IP laws and regulations; (d) establishment of government-to-government cooperative mechanisms. Measured and reported per prioritized country set (example: Brazil, China, India) with targets (e.g., 66%) and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number Trained on Best Practices to Protect and Enforce IP (GIPA output)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of people, including foreign government officials and U.S. stakeholders, trained on best practices to protect and enforce IP through GIPA programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output metric measuring training reach and capacity building; includes number of programs delivered and participants trained (example FY2023 target 5,000 vs actual >10,000); used to assess international and domestic training effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Satisfaction with Designated Priority Services (Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of customers who indicate positive satisfaction with designated priority services in the Patents program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customer satisfaction measured for priority services as an outcome indicator; used alongside other trust/confidence and net promoter score metrics to evaluate service quality and customer experience (details and targets provided in dashboard/appendix).
